text: The High Court rejected terra nullius and recognised native title. The Court held that Indigenous Australians have rights to land based on traditional laws and customs, provided those rights have not been extinguished. Native title is recognised by the common law and may coexist with other interests.

Established the modern law of negligence. A manufacturer owes a duty of care to the ultimate consumer where harm is reasonably foreseeable. Lord Atkin formulated the neighbour principle: one must take reasonable care to avoid acts or omissions which can reasonably be foreseen to injure one's neighbour.

case_name: Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co
text: The Court held that a unilateral offer can be accepted by performance. The advertisement constituted a binding offer, and performance of the conditions amounted to acceptance. Consideration was provided through the inconvenience suffered by the plaintiff.

case_name: Amalgamated Society of Engineers v Adelaide Steamship Co Ltd
text: Established that constitutional interpretation should follow ordinary principles of statutory interpretation. Rejected implied immunities and reserved state powers doctrines.
Confirmed the implied freedom of political communication and established a structured test to assess whether a law impermissibly burdens that freedom.

Established the test for breach of duty. A risk is foreseeable if it is not far-fetched or fanciful, and the court balances probability, seriousness, burden of precautions, and utility of the activity.
The High Court held that damages for disappointment and distress are generally not recoverable in contract unless the contract is for enjoyment or relaxation.
Established that a company is a separate legal entity distinct from its shareholders, even if controlled by a single individual.
Established the strict rule that fiduciaries must not profit from their position without informed consent, even where the principal could not have obtained the benefit.
Confirmed that jurisdictional error cannot be excluded by privative clauses and that courts retain the power to review unlawful administrative action.
